correctness.rationale: For real α>−1 in the complex-valued harmonic Bergman L²((α+1)(1−|z|²)^α dA/π), the Fourier monomials e_n produce a bilateral weighted shift, positive weights w_n→1 in both tails, ||T||=1, inverse powers of polynomial norm growth, hence spectrum is exactly the unit circle. For r<1, the inverse Laurent series converges in operator norm. Its analytic-to-antianalytic block is exactly rank one with entries r^(m+j−1)/sqrt(m_m m_j); sum 1/m_n=(1−r²)^−(α+2) gives norm r^−1(1−r²)^−(α+2)sqrt(1−(1−r²)^(α+2)). The remaining two within-half-line blocks have ||·||=O((1−r)^−(α+3)/2), strictly smaller than the cross block because α>−1; hence the sharp interior limit 2^−(α+2) after scaling by (1−r)^(α+2). The outer norm equals 1/(r−1) by ||T||=1 and spectral radius lower bound. Fourier rotation invariance and inversion give the stated asymmetric pseudospectral radial depths. Independent reconstructed truncated matrices checked rank-one norm and positive block tail formula for 12 α,r configurations; finite sections are not infinite operator estimates. Pseudospectral statement assumes the stated resolvent convention; α=−1 excluded.
